clue.text: Apostle unknown to give church offence

parts.note: Simon (Peter) was one of the twelve apostles
in algebra Y stands for an unknown quantity

explanation.surface: A disciple and a mystery person combine to upset the clergy.
explanation.definitionFit: Simony is the sin of buying or selling church offices or privileges, an ecclesiastical offence.

clue.text: Medicine case after some contents removed

indicators.note: the case comes after the trimmed word
the inner letters of the word some are taken away, leaving its ends

parts.note: the dative is a grammatical case

explanation.surface: A box of pills after some of them have been taken out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' suggests a container, but it is the grammatical case DATIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: A sedative is a calming drug, a kind of medicine.

clue.text: Intend keeping in King's mistress around for ages

indicators.note: around means turned round, so the whole is read backwards
the intend word holds the next pieces inside it

parts.note: to aim is to intend
taken as written
Nell Gwyn was the mistress of King Charles II

explanation.surface: A royal mistress hangs on for ages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeping' and 'around' both work on the whole: the inner pieces sit inside before the full run is read backwards. Nell Gwyn was Charles II's mistress.
explanation.definitionFit: Millennia are thousand-year periods, so ages in the sense of very long times.

clue.text: Puzzle negative apparently

definitions.meaning: read playfully, ... looks like not positive, so negative

explanation.surface: A riddle that seems to be a no.
explanation.definitionFit: To nonplus someone is to perplex them so they do not know how to respond.

clue.text: It helps to pick fruit to cover each tart alternately

indicators.note: the fruit is wrapped around the other letters, covering them

parts.note: a plum is a fruit

indicators.note: every other letter is taken from the words each and tart

explanation.surface: A kitchen tip about topping a tart with fruit to help you choose it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'alternately' works on both words at once, taking the first and third letters of each; 'to cover' means the fruit surrounds them.
explanation.definitionFit: A plectrum is the small flat tool a guitarist uses to pick or strum the strings.

clue.text: Aliens landed — let out by environmentalists

parts.note: lit is a past tense of light, to land or alight

indicators.note: out means disordered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: greens are environmentalists, so green men

explanation.surface: Aliens touch down and are freed by eco-campaigners.
explanation.definitionFit: Little green men is a jocular phrase for extraterrestrials.

clue.text: Person in charge, mean fellow, upset work schedule

parts.note: a cur is a contemptible man

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so read backwards

parts.note: a rota is a schedule of work shifts

explanation.surface: A nasty boss upsets the staff timetable.
explanation.definitionFit: A curator is the keeper in charge of a museum or collection.

clue.text: Soften having sacked indefinite number and hire again

indicators.note: sacked means dismissed, so a letter is removed

parts.note: to relent is to soften one's attitude
N stands for an indefinite number in maths

explanation.surface: A softening boss sacks some staff and then rehires.
explanation.definitionFit: To relet is to rent out again, as a landlord hires out property once more.

clue.text: Home Secretary's border chaos

parts.note: Theresa May was Home Secretary when this puzzle appeared
a hem is the border of a garment

explanation.surface: Turmoil at the frontier blamed on the minister for home affairs.
explanation.definitionFit: Mayhem means violent disorder or chaos.

clue.text: Output of Brahms etc — miss one to soothe us entertained by highest of the brass

indicators.note: the pieces are held inside the commander

parts.note: the commander-in-chief, CIC, is the most senior of the top brass
a lass is a young girl or miss
I is the Roman numeral one
to calm is to soothe

explanation.surface: A girl soothed by a top brass player performing Brahms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'highest of the brass' is military slang: the top brass are senior officers, the highest being the commander-in-chief.
explanation.definitionFit: Brahms wrote symphonies and concertos, works of classical music.

clue.text: Lady Gaga fronts new singer-songwriter

indicators.note: the anagram stands in front of the next piece
gaga means crazy or confused, so the letters of the word before are jumbled

explanation.surface: Lady Gaga leads the way for a fresh singing talent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lady Gaga' reads as the pop star, but 'Gaga' scrambles LADY into DYLA, which 'fronts' N.
explanation.definitionFit: Bob Dylan is the celebrated American singer-songwriter.

clue.text: Improvement towards end of game from one side

parts.note: something late in a match comes towards its end
a rally is a recovery or improvement in fortunes

explanation.surface: A team recovers in the closing stages of a match, coming in from the wing.
explanation.definitionFit: Laterally means sideways, so something moving laterally comes from one side.

clue.text: Report is about resistance supporter

indicators.note: the report-plus-is pair goes around the next letter

parts.note: to tell is to report or relate
R is the symbol for electrical resistance
taken as written

explanation.surface: A news story about someone backing the resistance movement.
explanation.definitionFit: A trellis is a lattice frame that supports climbing plants.

clue.text: Title Beatles' leading pair composed

indicators.note: composed means put together or arranged, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
the first two letters of Beatles are B and E

explanation.surface: A song name penned by the two leading Beatles, Lennon and McCartney.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composed' shuffles TITLE and BE into the title of the song.
explanation.definitionFit: Let It Be is a song credited to Lennon and McCartney, the Beatles' leading pair, so the whole clue describes it.

clue.text: It improves appearance saving chairmen in trouble

indicators.note: letters in trouble are disturbed, so they are reordered

explanation.surface: A rescue plan for company bosses who have got into difficulties.
explanation.definitionFit: Vanishing cream is a cosmetic that sinks into the skin, used to improve the complexion.

clue.text: Fearsome beast dismembered gorilla and ate two-thirds

indicators.note: dismembered means torn apart, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: two thirds of the word ate is its first two letters

explanation.surface: A savage creature tore apart a gorilla and devoured most of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two-thirds' takes AT from 'ate'; 'dismembered' mixes GORILLA and AT.
explanation.definitionFit: The alligator is a large, dangerous reptile.

clue.text: Plan with arsenic involved coming to naught

indicators.note: involved means tangled, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: naught means zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A poisoning plot comes to nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A scenario is an outline or projected plan of events.

clue.text: Badly ruled country not covered outside nanny state

indicators.note: the uncovered word wraps around the nanny

parts.note: bare means uncovered
nana is an informal word for a grandmother or nanny
public means of the state, as in public sector

explanation.surface: A comment on a poorly governed land run as an interfering nanny state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nanny state' reads as one phrase in the surface, but it splits into two pieces, nanny and state.
explanation.definitionFit: A banana republic is a small, unstable, corruptly governed country.

clue.text: White Hart Lane's rarely welcoming them — the reverse

indicators.note: the letters are read in the opposite direction
the letters are taken from inside the words Lane's rarely, which welcome them

explanation.surface: Tottenham's ground seldom hosts its local rivals.
explanation.walkthrough: White Hart Lane was Tottenham Hotspur's ground; 'welcoming' takes LANESRA from 'Lane's rarely' and 'the reverse' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: From the Tottenham viewpoint of White Hart Lane, the north London rival club is them.

clue.text: Peacekeepers provided men — mark what they wear

parts.note: UN peacekeepers serve the United Nations
if means provided that
OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers or men
M is short for mark, the old German currency

explanation.surface: UN troops are issued with their kit.
explanation.definitionFit: A uniform is the standard clothing soldiers wear.

clue.text: Provoke heartless rider's support

indicators.note: the central letter is removed

parts.note: a stirrup supports a rider's foot

explanation.surface: A rider's foot-rest has lost its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: To stir up trouble is to provoke it.

clue.text: Cross member of Parliament's last to redeem

indicators.note: the final letter of the word Parliament is taken

parts.note: to ransom is to pay to redeem a captive

explanation.surface: An angry MP's final effort to buy something back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross member of Parliament' suggests an angry MP, but 'Cross member' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A transom is a horizontal crossbar, as above a door or window.

clue.text: Provide access to Cambridge college after present era

indicators.note: the college comes after the era

parts.note: AD, anno Domini, denotes the present era
MIT is in Cambridge, Massachusetts

explanation.surface: A college admissions note about the modern age.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cambridge college' suggests the English university; it is MIT in the American Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: To admit is to let in, giving access.

clue.text: Cooking ling Una provides help for chippy

indicators.note: cooking suggests something being mixed, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Una frying ling helps out at the fish and chip shop.
explanation.walkthrough: A chippy is British slang for both a fish and chip shop and a carpenter; here it is the carpenter.
explanation.definitionFit: A nail gun is a power tool that drives nails, an aid to a carpenter.

clue.text: Recount memories about old cars with Civil Engineer

parts.note: re means about or concerning
the Mini is a classic old British car

explanation.surface: An engineer telling stories about classic cars.
explanation.definitionFit: To reminisce is to talk over past memories.

clue.text: River dweller heading off wizard

indicators.note: the first letter is removed

parts.note: Harry Potter is the boy wizard

explanation.surface: A creature living by the water chases off a magician.
explanation.definitionFit: The otter is an aquatic mammal living along rivers.

clue.text: Old TV game show featuring proverbial name-caller and his insult

parts.note: in the proverb the pot calls the kettle black
the pot's insult to the kettle is black

explanation.surface: A vintage programme recalls the old saying about hypocritical name-calling.
explanation.walkthrough: Pot Black was a BBC snooker programme, a staple of British TV from 1969.
explanation.definitionFit: Pot Black was a long-running televised snooker competition, a game show of sorts.

clue.text: Developing more by early stage

indicators.note: developing means changing form, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Getting more by being early in development.
explanation.definitionFit: An embryo is an organism at its earliest stage of development.
